title: Expose ingress queue depth percentiles and fix tenant label propagation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a capacity spike on 2025-03-09 we observed a multi-tenant latency regression in the Console ingestion path that was not surfaced by existing dashboards. Root cause analysis revealed two blind spots: 1) ingress queue depth was only exposed as an aggregate gauge and we had no per-tenant percentile metrics (p90/p95/p99), and 2) tenant_id propagation was intermittently dropped for retry paths, causing many traces and metrics to be unattributable to tenants which blocked fast correlation to impacted customers. This ticket captures action items to add percentile instrumentation, fix label propagation in the retry middleware, add dashboards/alerts, and a short retro to ensure deploy/rollback procedures cover metrics regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant ingress queue depth metrics exported (p50,p90,p95,p99) with the same scrape cadence as other ingress metrics
Trace spans emitted for retry middleware include tenant_id and request_id for all retry/async code paths
New dashboard tile for per-tenant queue depth percentiles is available in Console; grouping by tenant and route
Alert rule: sustained p99 queue depth > configured threshold for > 60s triggers PagerDuty and creates an investigative Playbook runbook link
E2E test added to verify tenant label persists across retry and fallback logic
Canary rollout plan executed and verified in staging before full deploy
tasks: Add histogram metrics to ingress worker (prometheus client): record queue duration and queue depth buckets - Liam
Audit and update retry middleware to attach tenant_id to spans and metric labels - Liam
Create new Console dashboard tiles: per-tenant queue percentiles, heatmap for top-10 tenants by p99 - Maya (Console PM)
Author alerting rules and add a runbook link for sustained queue percentile spikes - On-call SRE
Backfill script: run log-to-metrics job for the 2025-03-09 incident window to reconstruct per-tenant queue percentiles for RCA completeness - SRE
Add unit/integration tests that simulate dropped tenant labels and assert label persistence - Engineering QA
Canary rollout: staging -> small subset of tenants in dedicated cluster -> full rollout; monitor metrics for 30m at each stage - Release Eng
links: Runbook draft for queue percentile alerts: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Queue+Percentile+Runbook
comments: 2025-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after PM/Oncall sync. Immediate remediation prioritized: instrument percentiles and prevent tenant label loss. Assigned to Liam for code fixes.

2025-03-11 - Liam Chen: Identified that the ingress queue is currently measured only as a gauge updated on push/pop. Will replace with a prometheus histogram to get percentiles, and will add a light-weight label attach on enqueuing. Estimated 8 points.
2025-03-12 - Maya Patel (PM): Console will need a heatmap for tenant p99 and an overview tile for ‘Top 10 tenants by p99 queue’. I’ll own the dashboard design and QA sign-off.

2025-03-12 - SRE Oncall (Jorge Ruiz): Backfill script approved to run against archived logs; will attempt to reconstruct p95/p99 for the incident window to improve customer RCA. Will coordinate with Privacy for log access.

2025-03-13 - Liam Chen: Opened two PRs for metrics and middleware. Running unit tests locally; integration tests failing intermittently due to sampling config. Investigating test flakiness related to histogram bucket boundaries.

2025-03-14 - Ava Martinez: Scheduled canary Tuesday 2025-03-18. Add a checklist to PR template to verify label propagation and dashboard ingestion before merge. Action: SRE to wire canary alert group to PagerDuty escalation policy.

2025-03-14 - Note: we observed a related telemetry gap where long-tail tenant spikes coincided with a config change that reduced sampling of retry traces. Follow-up ticket suggested to re-evaluate sampling budget allocation (will create ENG follow-up).
notes: Trade-offs: adding per-tenant percentiles increases metrics cardinality. To mitigate, we'll emit percentiles only for tenants above a traffic threshold and add a sampled 'all-tenants' histogram for aggregate trends.
Mitigation window: if immediate rollout isn't possible, we will enable temporary coarse bucketing and tight retention for high-sensitivity metrics to preserve storage costs.

Observation: tenant label loss primarily occurred during the async retry codepath when a context copy omitted metadata. This is low-risk to fix but requires careful testing across language boundaries (Go ingress, Node retry proxy).
